recent_posts.title: Three TSConfig options you should enable in every TypeScript project
recent_posts.summary: Three useful TypeScript compiler options worth enabling in every project: `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` (forces null checks when accessing array elements by index), `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` (requires break/return in switch cases), and `allowUnreachableCode` (warns about unreachable code). All three improve type safety and help catch bugs and typos early.

recent_posts.title: Build a habit tracker app to learn React fundamentals
recent_posts.summary: A beginner-friendly walkthrough for building a habit tracking app with React and TypeScript using Vite as the bundler and Tailwind CSS for styling. Covers all major React fundamentals including JSX, components, props, children, conditional rendering, list rendering with keys, and component variants. The tutorial progresses from project setup through creating reusable components (Button, Header, HabitForm, HabitList, HabitItem), handling date ranges with the date-fns library, and using TypeScript's ComponentProps to forward HTML attributes to custom components.

TypeScript const generics for automatic literal type inference
recent_posts.summary: TypeScript has an undocumented feature called const generics, which lets you add the `const` keyword before a generic type parameter. This automatically applies `as const` semantics to any value passed into the function, giving you the strictest possible literal type inference without requiring callers to manually append `as const` at every call site. The example demonstrates a generic `first()` function that, without const generics, infers a return type of `number` instead of the specific literal union `1 | 2 | 3`.

recent_posts.title: Zustand crash course from basics to real world usage
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive crash course on Zustand, a lightweight state management library for React. Covers migrating from React Context to Zustand, setting up a store with TypeScript, using selectors for performance optimization, the useShallow hook to avoid infinite loops, accessing state outside React components, organizing actions separately from state, persisting state to localStorage with the persist middleware, and simplifying nested state updates with Immer.

recent_posts.title: How to use TypeScript path aliases for cleaner imports
recent_posts.summary: TypeScript's tsconfig `paths` compiler option lets you define import aliases to avoid long relative import paths. By mapping a shorthand like `@/` to your source directory, you can use absolute-style imports throughout your project. You also need to enable the corresponding setting in your bundler — for Vite, set `resolve.tsconfigPaths` to true — to ensure the aliases are respected at build time.

recent_posts.title: Building a UI in 10 minutes with CSS vs AI
recent_posts.summary: A developer attempts to recreate a UI design using only CSS in 10 minutes as part of a timed challenge on CSSBattle-style platform. The walkthrough covers planning the layout using flexbox, applying CSS variables for colors, styling score rows with dotted borders, and fine-tuning typography and spacing. After achieving a 73% match manually, the author tests the same challenge with AI, which scores only 61% and produces quirky artifacts like unnecessary linear gradients, hardcoded pixel values, and ignored CSS variable instructions — concluding that AI is a useful starting point but not a reliable replacement for hands-on CSS skills.

recent_posts.title: How to use useSyncExternalStore to sync browser state in React
recent_posts.summary: A practical walkthrough of React's useSyncExternalStore hook as an alternative to useEffect for syncing external browser state into React. Covers three use cases: tracking navigator.onLine status, syncing HTML dialog element open/close state (including keyboard escape handling), and building a lightweight global store similar to Zustand or Redux without Context. Explains the hook's subscribe/snapshot/server-snapshot parameters and shows how to avoid common pitfalls like stale state references.

recent_posts.title: How the CSS corner-shape property works with practical examples
recent_posts.summary: The new CSS `corner-shape` property lets developers control the shape of border-radius corners beyond the default rounded style. It supports keyword values like `round`, `scoop` (inverted radius), `bevel` (straight line), `square` (no radius), and `notch` (inverted square), as well as a `super-ellipse()` function accepting values from negative to positive infinity for fine-grained control. Practical use cases include ticket/badge shapes, speech bubbles, slotted UI elements, and animated shape transitions. Individual corners can be targeted independently. The main limitation is browser support at ~66%, with no support in Safari or Firefox yet, though graceful fallback makes it usable for decorative purposes.

This Folder Structure Makes Me 100% More Productive
top_posts.summary: A well-organized folder structure can significantly enhance code maintainability and enjoyment in development. This structure is applicable across various types of development, regardless of the language or framework used. By demonstrating with diagrams and real-world examples, the benefits of transitioning from a traditional folder layout to a feature-based structure are highlighted. ESLint configurations enforce these practices, making collaborative projects more manageable and helping keep each feature's code isolated, facilitating easier modifications and refactoring.

top_posts.title: Effective Code Structuring Using Adapter and Facade Patterns
top_posts.summary: Learn how to structure your code effectively using adapter and facade patterns to simplify database queries and improve maintainability in large projects. Kyle from Web Dev Simplified compares two project structures, showing the pros and cons of each approach, and highlights the importance of centralizing code and creating abstractions to make refactoring and library changes easier.

top_posts.title: Understanding background jobs and job queuing systems
top_posts.summary: Understanding and implementing background jobs or job queuing systems can significantly optimize server performance by offloading non-critical tasks from the main request flow. This concept allows tasks such as sending emails or saving information to a file-based system to be processed in the background, reducing the wait time for users. The post explains the architecture and implementation of a Redis-based job queue system, including priority handling, delayed jobs, and retry mechanisms.

top_posts.title: Must Have VSCode Extension For TypeScript Devs
top_posts.summary: The Pretty TypeScript Better Type Previews extension for VSCode helps TypeScript developers by providing expanded type information when hovering over variables or types. This facilitates understanding complex types without tracking down type definitions manually, making development more efficient.
